ei.subject: 영어1
ei.title: Endurance on the Endurance / Wounded Healer

fullPassage:
On August 1, 1914, Ernest Shackleton departed London on the ship Endurance with 27 men and 69 dogs to cross the Antarctic continent. Little did they know the journey ahead would be one of the most challenging adventures in history.
The crew members were full of excitement, but when their ship got stuck in thick pack ice on January 18, 1915, their joy quickly turned to fear. "Oh, my! It's frozen like an almond in the middle of a chocolate bar!" cried one of the crew members. Shackleton and his men had to abandon their ship and set up camp on the floating ice, where they would be forced to spend the winter. Each man was given a sleeping bag and was assigned to one of five tents. Shackleton yielded the better sleeping bags to other crew members and chose to stay with the group's more troublesome characters who could get involved in conflicts. The camping mats were not waterproof, so they were constantly wet. The men shivered in the severe cold and suffered from frostbite. Worst of all, the floating ice on which they were camped began cracking beneath them. Shackleton walked around inspecting the ice regularly for the crew members' safety. Some nights, Shackleton and his men had to pick up their tents, moving their camp to a more secure area where the ice was less likely to break.
Days went by, and all the crew members could see for miles around was ice. Despite the hopeless situation, Shackleton tried to make the crew at ease with his humor. A crew member even played his banjo to relieve the crew members' anxiety and depression. Seldom were they happy, though. In the rare happy moments, music became a kind of mental medicine. Shackleton's open and honest communication was helpful to the crew members.
The crew members struggled in the hope of getting back on the Endurance one day, but that day would never come. "She's going, boys!" Shackleton shouted on the evening of November 21, 1915, witnessing his ship finally breaking up and sinking into the Weddell Sea.
The 28 men were now isolated on drifting ice hundreds of miles from land, with no ship, no means of communication with the outside world, and limited supplies. Realizing the need for a new survival plan, Shackleton established daily routines for his men. The crew members began each day with breakfast and performed daily tasks such as hunting for food and making improvements to the three lifeboats which were previously rescued from the sunken ship. Time was also set aside for activities like reading or exercising. The crew sang songs, celebrated their crew members' birthdays, and even played football matches on the ice. Even in these occasional moments of joy, at night, the men had to take turns watching for any ice breaking beneath their feet.
On April 9, 1916, the floating ice began to crack, and Shackleton gave the order: "Launch the boats." They traveled across the sea ice and then the open water. They fought against freezing sea water pouring into the boats before they finally reached Elephant Island 6 days later, on April 15. The island was far from any shipping routes, so they were not likely to be found and rescued.
On April 20, with four crew members, Shackleton set off on a risky journey in a small lifeboat to seek help from a whaling station on South Georgia Island, which was 1,300 km away. He took some of the troublesome characters with him so that the remaining crew would not fight while on Elephant Island. Each morning on the island, Frank Wild, whom Shackleton had left in charge, called everyone to be ready to depart. "The Boss may come today!" he declared daily.
Shackleton and the four crew members finally reached South Georgia Island on May 10. Still, their struggle was not over yet. The whaling station was located on the other side of a mountain range. They had to cross the rocky mountains on foot. They stopped to rest for a while, and the exhausted men fell asleep right away. Shackleton woke them up after only a five-minute nap, which saved them from freezing to death. When they arrived at the whaling station, Shackleton hurried to arrange for a rescue ship, the Yelcho, to be sent to Elephant Island.
On August 30, 1916, the crew members on Elephant Island spotted a ship. Upon hearing the news of the rescue ship's arrival, everyone rushed out of camp. "Are you alright?" Shackleton called out. "All well!" came the reply. All 28 men on the island were rescued alive and safe. After 634 days of drifting in the Antarctic, the crew had finally reached the end of their long and harsh journey.
"I have done it," Shackleton wrote to his wife. "Not a life lost, and we have been through hell."
A Swiss psychologist, Carl Jung, is credited with coining the term "a wounded healer." He stated that "We don't get wounded alone, and we don't heal alone." Then what does "a wounded healer" mean? Wounded healers are people whose painful experiences enable them to help others. They are good listeners and view all experiences as opportunities to understand others' hardships. Indeed, one should be wounded to become a healer. People who go through suffering do not always become healers. It is those who overcome suffering who can become wounded healers, and they can evolve into "wounded leaders." The wounded leaders are those who understand wounds and learn from them. In fact, wounds in leadership would be transformative because they lead to deeper self knowledge, stronger relationships, and greater leadership skills. Leaders who have dealt with their wounds find themselves more at peace. Therefore, their leadership style is characterized by the ability to embrace the uncomfortable but necessary process of healing: accepting different perspectives and focusing on personal development while pursuing their goals.

questions.passage: Shackleton and his men had to (A)[abandon / board] their ship and set up camp on the (B)[floating / sinking] ice, where they would be forced to spend the winter. The men shivered in the (C)[severe / mild] cold and suffered from frostbite.
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: Shackleton과 대원들은 배를 버리고(abandon) 떠다니는(floating) 얼음 위에 캠프를 차려야 했다. 대원들은 혹독한(severe) 추위에 떨며 동상에 걸렸다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① abandoned–floating–severe: 모두 원문 그대로 적합
❌ ② sinking은 floating의 반의어, mild는 severe의 반의어
❌ ③ boarded는 abandon의 반의어 (배에 승선하다)
❌ ④ 전부 반의어로 구성
det.tip: abandon(버리다) ↔ board(승선하다) / floating(떠다니는) ↔ sinking(가라앉는) / severe(혹독한) ↔ mild(온화한)

questions.passage: The 28 men were now (A)[isolated / connected] on drifting ice hundreds of miles from land, with no ship, no means of communication with the outside world, and (B)[limited / abundant] supplies. Realizing the need for a new survival plan, Shackleton (C)[established / disrupted] daily routines for his men.
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 28명의 대원들은 유빙 위에 고립되어(isolated) 보급품도 제한되어(limited) 있었다. Shackleton은 일과를 정했다(established).
det.analysis:
✅ ① isolated–established–limited: 모두 원문 적합
❌ ② connected–disrupted–abundant: 전부 반의어
❌ ③ isolated는 맞지만 disrupted–abundant가 부적합
❌ ④ connected가 부적합
det.tip: isolated(고립된) ↔ connected(연결된) / established(수립하다) ↔ disrupted(방해하다) / limited(제한된) ↔ abundant(풍부한)

questions.passage: In fact, wounds in leadership would be (A)[transformative / destructive] because they lead to deeper self knowledge, stronger relationships, and greater leadership skills. Their leadership style is characterized by the ability to (B)[embrace / reject] the uncomfortable but necessary process of healing: accepting different perspectives and focusing on personal development while (C)[pursuing / abandoning] their goals.
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 상처는 리더십에서 변화를 가져올(transformative) 것이다. 불편하지만 필수적인 치유 과정을 포용(embrace)하고, 목표를 추구(pursuing)하면서.
det.analysis:
✅ ① transformative–embrace–pursuing: 모두 원문 적합
❌ ② transformative는 맞지만 reject–abandoning이 부적합
❌ ③ destructive–reject: 전부 반의어
❌ ④ destructive와 abandoning이 반의어
det.tip: transformative(변혁적인) ↔ destructive(파괴적인) / embrace(포용하다) ↔ reject(거부하다) / pursuing(추구하는) ↔ abandoning(포기하는)

questions.passage: The crew members were full of ①<u>excitement</u>, but when their ship got stuck in thick pack ice, their joy quickly turned to fear. Shackleton and his men had to ②<u>abandon</u> their ship and set up camp on the floating ice. Shackleton yielded the better sleeping bags to other crew members and chose to stay with the group's more ③<u>reliable</u> characters who could get involved in conflicts. The camping mats were not ④<u>waterproof</u>, so they were constantly wet.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 대원들은 ①설렘으로 가득했다. 배를 ②버려야 했다. 갈등을 일으킬 수 있는 더 ③믿을 만한→골칫거리(troublesome) 대원들과 함께 지냈다. 매트는 ④방수가 되지 않았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ reliable(믿을 만한)이 부적절 → 원문은 troublesome(골칫거리의). 갈등을 일으킬 수 있는 인물이므로 troublesome이 맞음.
❌ ① excitement: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ② abandon: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ④ waterproof: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: troublesome(골칫거리의) ↔ reliable(믿을 만한). 문맥 단서: 'get involved in conflicts'가 troublesome의 근거

questions.passage: Days went by, and all the crew members could see for miles around was ice. Despite the ①<u>hopeless</u> situation, Shackleton tried to make the crew at ②<u>ease</u> with his humor. A crew member even played his banjo to ③<u>intensify</u> the crew members' anxiety and depression. Seldom were they happy, though. In the rare happy moments, music became a kind of ④<u>mental</u> medicine.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ①절망적인 상황에서 Shackleton은 유머로 대원들을 ②편안하게 해 주었다. 한 대원은 불안감을 ③강화하기→덜어주기(relieve) 위해 밴조를 연주했다. 음악은 ④정신적인 약이 되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ intensify(강화하다)가 부적절 → 원문은 relieve(덜어주다). 밴조 연주의 목적은 불안감 해소.
❌ ① hopeless: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ② ease: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ④ mental: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: relieve(덜어주다) ↔ intensify(강화하다). 문맥 단서: 'to make the crew at ease'와 같은 맥락

questions.passage: Wounded healers are people whose painful experiences enable them to help others. They are good listeners and view all experiences as ①<u>obstacles</u> to understand others' hardships. Indeed, one should be wounded to become a healer. People who go through suffering do not always become healers. It is those who ②<u>overcome</u> suffering who can become wounded healers, and they can ③<u>evolve</u> into "wounded leaders." The wounded leaders are those who understand wounds and ④<u>learn</u> from them.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 상처 입은 치유자는 모든 경험을 다른 사람들의 어려움을 이해할 수 있는 ①장애물→기회(opportunities)로 여긴다. 고통을 ②극복하는 사람들이 치유자가 될 수 있으며, '상처 입은 리더'로 ③발전할 수 있다. 상처를 이해하고 ④배우는 사람이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① obstacles(장애물)이 부적절 → 원문은 opportunities(기회). 치유자는 경험을 '기회'로 보는 것이 맥락에 맞음.
❌ ② overcome: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ③ evolve: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ④ learn: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: opportunities(기회) ↔ obstacles(장애물). 문맥 단서: 'good listeners'이므로 경험을 긍정적으로 바라봄

questions.passage: The crew members were full of excitement, but when their ship got stuck in thick pack ice on January 18, 1915, their joy quickly turned to fear. Shackleton and his men had to __________ their ship and set up camp on the floating ice, where they would be forced to spend the winter. Each man was given a sleeping bag and was assigned to one of five tents. Shackleton yielded the better sleeping bags to other crew members and chose to stay with the group's more troublesome characters who could get involved in conflicts.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 배가 두꺼운 총빙에 갇혔을 때, Shackleton과 대원들은 배를 버리고(abandon) 떠다니는 얼음 위에 캠프를 차려야 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② abandoned: 배가 얼음에 갇혀 움직일 수 없으므로 버려야 함
❌ ① departed: 출발하다 — 배에서 나가는 것이지만 '버리다'의 뜻이 아님
❌ ③ repaired: 수리하다 — 얼음에 갇힌 배를 수리하는 것은 맥락에 안 맞음
❌ ④ decorated: 장식하다 — 무관
det.tip: abandon: 어쩔 수 없이 버리다, 포기하다. 위급 상황에서 배·건물을 떠나는 맥락에 자주 사용

questions.passage: The camping mats were not waterproof, so they were constantly wet. The men shivered in the severe cold and suffered from frostbite. Worst of all, the floating ice on which they were camped began cracking beneath them. Shackleton walked around __________ the ice regularly for the crew members' safety. Some nights, Shackleton and his men had to pick up their tents, moving their camp to a more secure area where the ice was less likely to break.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 얼음이 갈라지기 시작했고, Shackleton은 대원들의 안전을 위해 정기적으로 얼음을 점검하며(inspecting) 돌아다녔다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ inspecting: 안전을 위해 얼음 상태를 점검하는 것이 맥락에 적합
❌ ① struggled: 고군분투하다 — walked around와 결합 부자연스러움
❌ ② drifted: 표류하다 — 사람이 주어일 때 의도적 점검의 뜻 아님
❌ ③ communicated: 소통하다 — 얼음을 대상으로 소통한다는 것은 부적합
det.tip: inspect: 점검하다, 검사하다. walk around ~ing: ~하면서 돌아다니다 (동시 동작)

questions.passage: A Swiss psychologist, Carl Jung, is __________ with coining the term "a wounded healer." He stated that "We don't get wounded alone, and we don't heal alone." Wounded healers are people whose painful experiences enable them to help others. They are good listeners and view all experiences as opportunities to understand others' hardships.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 스위스 심리학자 칼 융은 '상처 입은 치유자'라는 용어를 만든 것으로 알려져(credited) 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① credited: be credited with ~ing = ~한 것으로 인정받다. 용어를 '만든 것'으로 알려짐
❌ ② associated: be associated with = ~와 관련되다. 용어를 '만든 것'의 의미 부족
❌ ③ burdened: be burdened with = ~로 짐을 지다. 부정적 맥락
❌ ④ confronted: be confronted with = ~에 직면하다. 용어를 만든 것과 무관
det.tip: be credited with ~ing: ~한 것으로 인정받다/공을 돌리다. credit은 '공로를 인정하다'의 뜻

questions.passage: Little did they know the journey ahead would be one of the most <u>challenging</u> adventures in history.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>challenging</u>과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 그들은 앞으로의 여정이 역사상 가장 험난한(challenging) 모험 중 하나가 될 줄을 전혀 알지 못했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ tough: 힘든, 어려운 — challenging과 동의어
❌ ① gentle: 부드러운 — 반의어에 가까움
❌ ② freezing: 얼어붙는 — 남극 맥락에서 혼동 가능하지만 '도전적인'과는 다름
❌ ④ boring: 지루한 — 무관
det.tip: challenging = tough = difficult = demanding (힘든, 도전적인)

questions.passage: Each man was given a sleeping bag and was assigned to one of five tents. Shackleton <u>yielded</u> the better sleeping bags to other crew members and chose to stay with the group's more troublesome characters.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>yielded</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: Shackleton은 더 좋은 침낭을 다른 대원들에게 양보했다(yielded).
det.analysis:
✅ ① gave up: 양보하다, 포기하다 — yielded와 동의어
❌ ② held onto: 붙잡다, 고수하다 — 반의어
❌ ③ searched for: 찾다 — 무관
❌ ④ carried: 나르다 — 무관
det.tip: yield: (1) 양보하다 (2) 수확하다 (3) 굴복하다. 여기서는 '남에게 양보하다'의 뜻

questions.passage: In fact, wounds in leadership would be <u>transformative</u> because they lead to deeper self knowledge, stronger relationships, and greater leadership skills.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>transformative</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 리더십에서 상처는 더 깊은 자기 지식, 더 강한 관계, 더 큰 리더십 기술로 이어지기 때문에 변화를 가져오는(transformative) 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ life-changing: 인생을 바꾸는 — transformative와 가장 유사
❌ ① temporary: 일시적인 — 변화의 지속성과 반대
❌ ② revolutionary: 혁명적인 — 유사하지만 transformative보다 급진적 의미
❌ ③ harmful: 해로운 — 문맥상 긍정적 변화이므로 부적합
det.tip: transformative = life-changing = having the power to transform. 긍정적 변화를 강조하는 형용사

questions.passage: The 28 men were now <u>isolated</u> on drifting ice hundreds of miles from land, with no ship, no means of communication with the outside world, and limited supplies.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>isolated</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 28명의 대원들은 유빙 위에 고립되어(isolated) 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② connected: 연결된 — isolated(고립된)의 반의어
❌ ① stranded: 오도 가도 못하는 — isolated와 유사어
❌ ③ separated: 분리된 — isolated와 유사어
❌ ④ abandoned: 버려진 — isolated와 유사어
det.tip: isolated(고립된) ↔ connected(연결된). 오답이 모두 비슷한 뉘앙스여서 함정이 됨

questions.passage: Little did they know the journey ahead would be one of the most <u>challenging</u> adventures in history. The crew members were full of excitement, but when their ship got stuck in thick pack ice, their joy quickly turned to fear.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>challenging</u>과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 앞으로의 여정이 역사상 가장 험난한(challenging) 모험 중 하나가 될 줄을 전혀 알지 못했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ effortless: 힘들이지 않는 — challenging(힘든, 도전적인)의 반의어
❌ ① painful: 고통스러운 — challenging과 유사 뉘앙스
❌ ② joyful: 즐거운 — 감정적 반대이지 '도전적'의 반의어는 아님
❌ ④ simple: 단순한 — '어려운'의 반의어이지만 challenging의 핵심은 '힘이 드는'
det.tip: challenging(힘든, 도전적인) ↔ effortless(힘들이지 않는, 쉬운). simple은 '복잡하지 않은'이므로 뉘앙스 차이

questions.passage:
(A) On August 30, 1916, the crew members on Elephant Island <u>spotted</u> a ship.
(B) There was a dark <u>spot</u> on the ice where the oil had leaked from the sunken ship.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 의미로 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 대원들은 한 척의 배를 발견했다(spotted). (B) 기름이 새어 나온 곳에 어두운 얼룩(spot)이 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② (A) 발견하다 – (B) 얼룩: (A) spotted = 발견하다, (B) spot = 얼룩/점
❌ ① (B) 지점은 가능하지만 oil leaked → dark spot이므로 '얼룩'이 더 적합
❌ ③ 인식하다는 spotted의 의미로 부족 (먼 곳에서 '눈에 띄다')
❌ ④ 전부 부적합
det.tip: spot: (동사) 발견하다, 알아채다 / (명사) 지점, 장소, 얼룩. 문맥에 따라 판단

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
"injury to body tissues caused by exposure to extreme cold, typically affecting the nose, fingers, or toes"

det.korean: 극심한 추위에 노출되어 코, 손가락, 발가락 등 신체 조직이 손상되는 것 = 동상(frostbite)
det.analysis:
✅ ① frostbite: 동상 — 정의와 정확히 일치
❌ ② sunburn: 햇볕에 탄 것 — 추위가 아닌 자외선
❌ ③ heatstroke: 열사병 — 반대 기후 조건
❌ ④ dehydration: 탈수 — 수분 부족, 추위와 무관
det.tip: frostbite: frost(서리) + bite(물다) = 동상. 본문에서 대원들이 severe cold에서 suffered from frostbite

questions.passage: The 28 men were now isolated on drifting ice hundreds of miles from land, with no ship and limited supplies. Realizing the need for a new __________ (survive) plan, Shackleton established daily routines for his men.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 새로운 생존(survival) 계획이 필요하다는 것을 깨달았다.
det.analysis:
survive(동사) → survival(명사): a new __________ plan에서 빈칸은 plan을 수식하는 명사(복합명사 구조)
survival plan = 생존 계획
det.tip: survive(생존하다) → survival(생존) / survivor(생존자) / surviving(살아남은). 여기서는 명사형 survival

questions.passage: Leaders who have dealt with their wounds find themselves more at peace. Therefore, their leadership style is __________ (character) by the ability to embrace the uncomfortable but necessary process of healing.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 그들의 리더십 유형은 치유 과정을 포용할 수 있는 능력이 특징(characterized)이다.
det.analysis:
character(명사) → characterized(과거분사): is characterized by = ~이 특징이다 (수동태)
주어 'leadership style'이 '특징지어지는' 것이므로 수동태 과거분사
det.tip: be characterized by: ~이 특징이다. character → characterize(특징짓다) → characterized(과거분사/수동)

ch: set up camp on the floating ice
cross the rocky mountains on foot
seek help from a whaling station
questions.passage: They fought against freezing sea water pouring into the boats before they finally reached Elephant Island 6 days later, on April 15. The island was far from any shipping routes, so they were not likely to be found and rescued. On April 20, with four crew members, Shackleton set off on a risky journey in a small lifeboat to __________ on South Georgia Island, which was 1,300 km away. He took some of the troublesome characters with him so that the remaining crew would not fight while on Elephant Island.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Shackleton은 1,300km 떨어진 사우스 조지아 섬의 포경 기지의 도움을 받기(seek help from a whaling station) 위해 위험한 여정을 떠났다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ seek help from a whaling station: 원문 그대로 — 구조를 요청하기 위한 여정
❌ ① set up camp: 이전 단계에서의 행동
❌ ② cross the rocky mountains: 사우스 조지아 도착 후의 행동
❌ ④ celebrate birthdays: 유빙 위 일상의 일부, 이 여정의 목적이 아님
det.tip: seek help from = ~에서 도움을 구하다. whaling station = 포경 기지

ch: overcome suffering and learn from wounds
questions.passage: People who go through suffering do not always become healers. It is those who __________ who can become wounded healers, and they can evolve into "wounded leaders." The wounded leaders are those who understand wounds and learn from them. In fact, wounds in leadership would be transformative because they lead to deeper self knowledge, stronger relationships, and greater leadership skills.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 고통을 겪는 사람들이 항상 치유자가 되는 것은 아니다. 고통을 극복하고 상처로부터 배우는(overcome suffering and learn from wounds) 사람들이 치유자가 될 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② overcome suffering and learn from wounds: 원문의 핵심 메시지와 일치
❌ ① avoid painful experiences: 치유자가 되려면 고통을 피하는 것이 아님
❌ ③ stay away from leadership: 오히려 리더로 발전한다고 함
❌ ④ ignore the process of healing: 치유 과정을 무시하는 것은 반대
det.tip: overcome suffering = 고통을 극복하다. 원문 핵심: 고통 경험 → 극복 → 치유자 → 리더로 발전
